short: New attention-before-CTC decoder for lip reading, but one corpus, one run and no in-house CTC-only or attention-only baseline make it standard; against LRSW it is a tie.
position: LCANet [@xu2018lcanet] changes one component, the decoder (M06): an attention layer placed before a single CTC loss, plus highway layers. The design is new in lip reading (no cascade or hybrid among 57 sentence-level decoder studies before 2018-03), but it is standard: one corpus, one run, no seeds, and no in-house CTC-only or attention-only baseline. The gain over LipNet holds on GRID with overlapping speakers, 2.9% against 4.8% WER, and 5.6% without LipNet's language model [@assael2016lipnet]. Against LRSW it does not: that system reports only a GRID WER of 3.0% [@chung2017was], so "better CER" has no comparator and 2.9% against 3.0% from single runs is a tie. The multi-task baseline ranked last is the design of the best later result under the same protocol [@wu2024lcrmi]. M12 is standard: overlapped speakers only, one run.
